items.fullText: 삼성전자, ‘실리콘밸리 미래 통신 서밋 2026’ 개최 2026/10/15 AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 삼성전자가 현지시간 14일부터 15일까지 미국 실리콘밸리 마운틴뷰에서 글로벌 통신 업계 파트너들과 차세대 네트워크의 미래를 논의하는 자리를 마련한다. 삼성전자는 14일에 ‘파트너 데이(Partner Day)’를 진행했고, 15일에는 ‘실리콘밸리 미래 통신 서밋 2026(Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit 2026)’을 개최한다. ▲ 14일(현지시간) 미국 실리콘밸리 마운틴뷰에서 진행된 ‘파트너 데이’ 행사 전경. 이번 행사에는 주요 이동통신사∙제조사∙정부 기관∙학계 리더 등 100여 명의 통신 전문가들이 참석해 AI와 다가올 6G 시대 소프트웨어 기반의 네트워크 진화 방향과 통신 산업의 가치 창출을 위한 생태계 협력 방안을 논의한다. 또한, 삼성전자는 ‘AI 내재형 6G 네트워크’ 기술 개발 성과 등을 선보인다. AI 시대의 네트워크 가치 창출을 위한 글로벌 협력 14일 파트너 데이 참석자들은 AI기반 통신산업의 변화에 대응하기 위한 소프트웨어 기반 네트워크 전략과 생태계 차원의 협력 방안을 논의했다. 삼성전자는 기조연설을 통해 AI가 애플리케이션과 서비스를 넘어 인프라 전반을 변화시키면서, 100여 년간 이어진 통신 네트워크도 구조적으로 재편되고 있다고 설명했다. 특히, AI와 가상화를 융합한 차세대 네트워크는 기존의 한계를 넘어 인류가 상상해 온 새로운 방식의 커뮤니케이션을 실현하는 핵심 동력이 될 것이라고 강조했다. ▲ 14일(현지시간) 미국 실리콘밸리 마운틴뷰에서 진행된 ‘파트너 데이’에서 삼성전자 네트워크사업부장 김우준 사장이 기조연설을 하고 있다. 이후, 통신 업계의 집단지성을 모아 AI 시대 네트워크 진화 전략과 방향을 본격적으로 논의하는 시간을 가졌다. 패널 세션에서는 통신 사업자들이 AI 기반 미래 네트워크의 요구사항과 청사진을 공유하고, 제조사들은 AI와 가상화 네트워크 상용화 과정에서 축적한 경험을 나누며 통신 생태계의 지속적인 발전 방향을 논의했다. 또, 단순한 연결 서비스를 넘어 새로운 네트워크 기반 신규 서비스를 발굴해 새로운 사업 기회로 연결하기 위한 방안을 다각도로 모색했다. 삼성전자 네트워크사업부 전략마케팅팀장 박정호 부사장은 “AI 시대의 네트워크는 쏟아지는 신규 서비스의 다양한 요구를 읽고, 가상화를 기반으로 유연하게 변화하며 최적의 답을 제시하는 지능형 인프라로 진화하고 있다”며, “삼성전자는 글로벌 파트너들과 함께 가상화 네트워크의 대규모 상용화를 성공적으로 이뤄왔다. 여기에 앞선 AI 기술을 더해 통신 인프라를 새로운 성장 엔진으로 발전시키고, 업계가 함께 도약하는 길을 앞장서 열어 나가겠다”고 말했다. items.d: Janus Henderson CEO Ali Dibadj said the firm is energized by its move to private ownership and is using the flexibility to invest in people, technology including AI, new products and client service. items.t: Vanguard CIO Greg Davis on Market, Inflation Outlook
items.d: Vanguard President and CIO Greg Davis said the CPI report was one data point for markets and the Federal Reserve to assess, while noting inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target and the Fed still has work to do. Davis said Vanguard generally expects one to two rate hikes over the coming months, depending on incoming data. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: Ambrosia Energy will build a 10 GWh factory in Texas to make batteries for off-grid data centers
items.d: Startup Ambrosia Energy will build a massive factory to crank out batteries to augment solar panels, creating a round-the-clock clean power plant.
items.fullText: Ambrosia Energy has begun work on a massive, 10 gigawatt-hour battery factory near Austin, Texas, co-founder and CEO Ben Longmier announced onstage Tuesday at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco. “That allows us to build about a 300 megawatt power plant per year out at our field sites,” he said. The factory will occupy 150,000 square feet, and Longmier said that Ambrosia plans to reach full production in two to three years. The startup emerged from stealth in June to build power plants for data centers at a cost of $100 per megawatt hour. Longmier and his co-founder, Sara Spangelo, had settled on solar plus batteries as the cheapest option that’s the fastest to deploy. Solar panels power the load during the day and charge the batteries, which discharge at night and on cloudy days to keep the data center operating round the clock. Longmier and Spangelo previously founded the satellite constellation startup Swarm, which they sold to SpaceX. Ambrosia is also beginning work on its first commercial power plant in West Texas later this year, Longmier said. The facility will pair 300 megawatts of solar panels with 660 megawatt-hours of batteries to deliver 30 megawatts of continuous power, with a goal of 99.3% uptime. Even with “overbuilding” solar and batteries to deliver continuous uptime, Longmier said the company can be profitable at $100 per megawatt-hour, making it competitive with natural gas turbines that many hyperscalers are planning to use to power their data centers. Sections of Ambrosia’s first pilot-scale power plant have been operating continuously for more than 100 days, Longmier said. The pilot is capable of generating 200 kilowatts of electricity 24/7. To hit its cost targets, Ambrosia has been finding ways to simplify its components, including solar mounts and battery packs. items.t: Prismm helps banks keep inherited money in-house
items.d: With Prismm, account holders can give designated family members access to their accounts and documents ahead of time.
items.fullText: Meet Prismm , a startup that helps banks keep families’ money in-house after an account holder dies. It does this by building beneficiary and estate planning into accounts from day one, which makes the transfer of assets to heirs less complicated. Prismm is presenting its mission today on the Startup Battlefield stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 . Prismm was founded in 2020 by sisters Martha Underwood and Shella Sylla, who each have decades of experience in banking and finance. The pair came up with the idea for Prismm based on their own experience of seeing firsthand how difficult it can be to manage a family’s affairs in an emergency. Their father was hospitalized in 2017 after he fell while helping clear a tree from a neighbor’s roof following Hurricane Irma in Miami. Their mother, who had always relied on him to handle the family’s finances and paperwork, didn’t know where all the important documents and financial information were, and neither did they. Their father recovered, but the experience of not knowing how to access critical information stuck with them. That was the starting point for Prismm, but the idea really took shape three years later, when Underwood was working at a bank during the COVID-19 pandemic. She saw families come in after a loved one had died, scrambling to find accounts, understand bills, and figure out how to support the surviving spouse. Image Credits: Prismm “That’s when it hit us that this is an infrastructure problem, and as I started to dig deeper, we’ve created all of these platforms for wealth growth and tracking, but almost nothing for transition,” Underwood said in an interview with TechCrunch. “It’s still very much all manual. items.t: Ukraine accuses SpaceX of restricting Starlink, disrupting military amid Trump pressure
items.d: Ukrainian officials and military units accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of throttling a technology at the heart of their battlefield communications and drone operations.
items.fullText: War in Ukraine Ukraine says new Starlink restrictions disrupt military as it reels from intel gaps and Trump clash Ukrainian officials and military units accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of throttling a technology at the heart of their battlefield communications and drone operations. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Zelenskyy slams Trump over deal for Russian diesel 01:32 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 14, 2026, 8:51 AM EDT / Updated Oct. 14, 2026, 3:55 PM EDT By Abigail Williams , Dan De Luce , Gabe Gutierrez , Yuliya Talmazan and Jane Lytvynenko Ukraine has accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of undermining its ability to defend itself by limiting Starlink internet services as it reeled from intense Russian ballistic missile attacks that it said came without the usual warning from allies. Musk put the responsibility for the restrictions on President Donald Trump’s shoulders on social media , saying the military version of Starlink, called Starshield, is owned and controlled by the U.S. government. “Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” Musk said. A spokesperson for President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NBC News that the limitations remained in place late Wednesday. Facing pressure from Trump to halt strikes on Russia’s energy industry, Kyiv and its backers have worried that Washington could cut off battlefield support to try to force it into concessions at the negotiating table. Ukrainian officials and their European partners were already scrambling to understand the status of U.S. intelligence-sharing after the lack of alert ahead of two Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv this week, two Ukrainian and two European officials told NBC News. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces New Investments in the UK Startup Ecosystem UK organizations across healthcare, finance, local government and climate science are putting NVIDIA AI to work. October 13, 2026 by Anthony Hills 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Across industries, the U.K. is putting the full stack to work. T he scale of deployment is growing fast, from enterprises transforming their businesses to startups solving some of the planet’s hardest problems. NVIDIA is putting that principle into practice, including through a five-year, $250 million compute commitment to strengthen the U.K.’s agentic safety and security research. NVIDIA’s Investments in the UK NVIDIA has been investing in the U.K. startup ecosystem, supporting companies including Basecamp Research , Ineffable Intelligence , Synthesia , Wayve and many more. Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Boltz , Foresight , Hiverge, Prima Mente and Riverlane . Boltz , a London-based AI startup founded by MIT researchers, builds biomolecular models and AI agents that help scientists predict molecular structures and interactions, and design potential new medicines. Foresight, a London-based startup, helps owners of major infrastructure projects, including hyperscale data centers, predict completion dates, mitigate risks and accelerate time to revenue. Hiverge , a Cambridge-based AI startup founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Cambridge, builds an AI discovery engine that automatically writes and optimizes algorithms for tasks such as faster AI training and complex logistics planning. Prima Mente , a London-based AI biology startup, focuses on building biological foundation models to decode complex diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets, starting with Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and ALS.
